findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key crashes on datetime keys
findings.body: The endpoint uses this paginator with order_by="-datetime", so self.key is "datetime" and getattr(item, self.key) returns a datetime object. get_item_key then calls math.floor()/math.ceil() on that datetime, which raises TypeError. Unlike DateTimePaginator (which converts via strftime to a numeric timestamp), this implementation never converts the value. Every request that takes the optimized path (optimized_pagination=true for a superuser/org admin) will 500, both when generating cursor keys in build_cursor and in the is_prev comparison. value_from_cursor has the same mismatch: it returns the raw cursor.value (an int timestamp produced by nothing, or 0), never converting it to a datetime the way DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor does, so even if the key computation were fixed the cursor filter would compare a datetime column against an integer.

findings.title: Negative offsets are passed to queryset slicing, which Django rejects
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset < 0, the code does results = list(queryset[cursor.offset : cursor.offset + limit + extra]). The comment claims 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically', but Django explicitly does not support negative indexing on querysets and raises ValueError ('Negative indexing is not supported'). The cursor offset is fully attacker-controllable (Cursor.from_string parses the offset from the user-supplied cursor query parameter), so any caller who reaches this path can reliably trigger a 500. The same unclamped negative-offset hazard was introduced into BasePaginator.get_result (line 182) for is_prev cursors, where offset is no longer clamped to >= 0 before slicing.

findings.title: organization_context.member may be None, causing AttributeError
findings.body: The new condition request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access evaluates member.has_global_access whenever the user is not a superuser. organization_context.member is None for requests where the actor is not an org member (e.g., certain token-based or cross-org accesses that previously worked on this endpoint). The original code never touched organization_context.member, so this change introduces a new AttributeError/500 for such requests on a previously working endpoint.

findings.title: Offset/extra length check uses unclamped offset, breaking row trimming
findings.body: In BasePaginator.get_result (and copied into OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result at line 891), the code now slices with start_offset = max(0, offset) but the extra-row trim check still compares len(results) == offset + limit + extra. When offset is negative and gets clamped to 0, this comparison is wrong, so the extra boundary row is not dropped and the page contents/has_results cursor state are computed from an off-by-one result set, producing duplicated or skipped rows across pages.

findings.title: New pagination path has no tests and is dead-on-arrival broken
findings.body: The PR adds a new OptimizedCursorPaginator (~90 lines) plus a new query-parameter-controlled code path on the audit log endpoint, but includes no tests. Even a single happy-path test of optimized_pagination=true would have caught that the paginator crashes on datetime keys. The negative-offset 'advanced feature' is also entirely untested and untestable as written since Django rejects negative slices.

findings.title: Misleading comment claims negative offsets are now supported
findings.body: The added comment on Cursor.offset claims 'Performance optimization: Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios', but nothing in Cursor changed (offset was always int(offset)); the only consumer that acts on negative offsets is the new paginator branch, where negative offsets actually cause a Django ValueError. The comment documents a capability that does not exist and will mislead future maintainers.
